resources.string: Plug in the hub/adapter and turn on Ethernet tethering. You can still start: the servers listen on every network.
Waiting for the PS2… open OPL / NHDDL / Neutrino on the console.

Phone → USB-C hub/adapter with an Ethernet port → network cable → PS2.

Turn on Settings › Network › Hotspot & tethering › Ethernet tethering. The phone then hands out an IP on the cable.

Phone IP: %1$s
On the PS2: DHCP (OPL) or IP %2$s, mask 255.255.255.0.

No Ethernet tethering option? Some phones only have it on Android 11+ or custom ROMs (e.g. LineageOS). If the adapter is not recognized at all, try a powered hub.
Let it run in the background (battery)

Folder: a folder on the phone or the root of a USB drive (exFAT, FAT32 or NTFS) with DVD/, CD/, ART/… Works with SMB1, UDPFS and UDPBD (UDPBD sees the folder as a virtual exFAT disk).\n\nWhole USB drive (advanced): the app reads the drive directly over USB (must be exFAT or FAT32). Only UDPBD and UDPFS in block mode. Eject the drive in Settings › Storage before starting; after stopping, unplug and plug it back.

Normal: Android permissions. Since Android 11 the folder picker refuses the root of the internal storage — use the "Internal storage" button instead (it uses "all files access"). USB drives go through the picker, which is slower.

Root: reads any path (including /mnt/media_rw, the USB drive without the picker, faster). Needs Magisk/KernelSU; allow the app when asked.

Shizuku: like root, without root. Install and start the Shizuku app (wireless debugging or ADB), then pick Shizuku here and allow it.
⚠ tap the USB drive below again
Folders created. Put the .iso files in DVD (or CD).
How to set up the PS2

OPL / RiptOPL › Network Settings:
• IP Address Type: DHCP (or %2$s)
• Address: %1$s
• Port: %3$d
• Share: PS2SMB · User: guest · Password: empty
• ETH Start Mode: Auto; save and restart OPL.
RiptOPL with SMB2: same port and share; any user and password. The app answers SMB1 and SMB2 on the same port.

Faster than SMB. Serves the folder (and the virtual disk).

RiptOPL: use the same PS2 IP as in the network settings.

Block device: the PS2 sees an exFAT disk (the folder as a virtual disk, or the whole USB drive).

Neutrino: config/bsd-udpbd.toml → args = ["ip=%1$s"]
RiptOPL / XEB+: UDPBD device, with PS2 IP %1$s.

↳ Another app is already using this port (another SMB/PS2 server?). Close it or restart the phone.
↳ The hub\'s network adapter dropped for a moment. If it keeps happening: use a hub with its own power supply, check the USB-C plug, or try another hub/cable.
↳ The PS2 stopped answering mid-transfer: the cable/hub flickered, or the game froze on the console (try another mode or loader settings).
↳ If the game froze now, the connection dropped: check the cable, the hub power and that the phone screen-off/battery saver didn\'t cut the network.
↳ Failed to read the game file: USB drive loose or without power, folder access revoked, or a damaged file.
↳ That client isn\'t OPL: only SMB1 is supported (OPL and RiptOPL use SMB1).
↳ The root/Shizuku access stopped (Shizuku restarted, or root was revoked). Stop and start again.
⚠ No network on the cable. Check: hub plugged in and powered, cable in the PS2, Ethernet tethering on.
⚠ The PS2 (%1$s) is not on the cable network (%2$s). Its IP should look like %3$s; replies may go out through Wi-Fi.
⚠ Android may pause the server with the screen off. Tap \"Let it run in the background\".

Games in .zso and .cso show up to the PS2 as plain .iso, decompressed on the fly by the phone.

This lets NHDDL/Neutrino (UDPFS and UDPBD) run compressed games, which take much less space.

Over SMB the .zso goes as is, since OPL reads ZSO by itself and the cable carries fewer bytes. The .cso becomes .iso over SMB too.

If an .iso with the same name exists, the compressed one is hidden.

The game list updates by itself every time you open the app: it looks for PS2 (.iso, .zso, .cso) and PS1 (.VCD and .cue) games in the whole folder and reads each game code. Only new or changed files are read again.\n\nOrganize: creates the OPL folders, moves PS2 games into DVD/ (over 700 MB) or CD/ and PS1 games into POPS/ or EMBER/games/, setting up multi-disc. It shows everything before doing it.
Choose the games folder on the Server tab.

Download: looks up the cover of each game without one by its code (xlenore/ps2-covers database, needs internet on the phone) and saves it as ART/<code>_COV.png.

Convert: turns JPG/WebP/BMP/PNG in the ART folder into 8-bit PNG (256 colors), the format OPL and RiptOPL read without errors and load faster.

Size: 140×200 is the OPL standard; 280×400 is the RiptOPL standard.

Packs every PNG in the ART folder into one file, ART/art.tar (uncompressed). RiptOPL reads covers from it much faster than from hundreds of loose files (turn it on in Interface › Artwork Settings). The loose files stay, for regular OPL.\n\nRedo it after downloading new covers.

Compress: ISO → ZSO (LZ4), which takes less space. OPL reads ZSO directly; for NHDDL/Neutrino the app decompresses on the fly ("Serve ZSO/CSO as ISO" in Advanced). Before anything is deleted, the new ZSO is checked against the ISO.

Decompress: ZSO/CSO → ISO.

It may take a few minutes per game on a slower phone; you can use other apps meanwhile.
Compress %1$d game(s). Once checked, delete the original ISO to free space?
Decompress %1$d game(s). Afterwards, delete the compressed file?

RiptOPL › Network Settings:
• Protocol: HTTP
• Address: %1$s
• Port: 1100 (always fill it in: with 0 the loader uses different ports for the list and for the game)
• Base path: / (or blank)

Uses TCP: no lost packets on cheap hubs, unlike UDP. Read-only: no VMC over HTTP. Dual-layer DVD9 may not work because of a loader limit.

RiptOPL and Docmine17\'s OPL-HTTP read games.csv in different formats, and the server cannot tell which one is on the other end.\n\nLeave it off for RiptOPL. Turn it on only for Docmine17\'s OPL-HTTP: the list then uses the simple format (up to ~200 games, no commas in names) and ZSO goes compressed.

Neutrino (nfs: driver) and RiptOPL › NFS:
• Server: %1$s
• Port: 2049
• Export: / (or /ps2)

Uses TCP, like HTTP: sturdier on cheap hubs. Neutrino only reads DVDs over NFS; RiptOPL also writes VMCs (the file must already exist).

Checks that the folder has the files each loader needs:
• POPStarter (PS1): POPS.ELF, IOPRP252.IMG, POPS_IOX.PAK, POPSTARTER.ELF
• Ember (PS1): ember.elf and the 512 KiB bios.bin
• Neutrino: modules and config (when NHDDL loads over the network)
• OPL: DVD, CD, ART, CFG, VMC folders

It checks presence, size and whether ELFs are valid. Sony files (POPS and BIOS) do not come with the app: use your own.
Nothing to check yet (no POPS/, EMBER/ or NEUTRINO/).
The loader of their format (VCD → POPS, CUE/BIN → Ember)

POPStarter: POPS/<game>.VCD. Multi-disc gets POPS/<disc>/DISCS.TXT (swap with Select+L2+R2) and VMCDIR.TXT (every disc saves to disc 1's card). Swaps between at most 4 discs.

Ember: EMBER/games/<game>/ with the .cue, the .bin files and the LibCrypt .sbi. Multi-disc stays in one folder with Discs.txt (swap from Ember's menu, same card).

CUE/BIN → VCD conversion produces the same file as CUE2POPS and accepts CUEs with several .bin files (Redump). A warning always comes before converting.
Organize automatically when the app opens (asks before converting)

🔒 The folder is read-only (NTFS drives usually are on Android, even with root). The PS2 reads the games normally, but the app cannot write covers, art.tar, compress or organize. For that, format the drive as exFAT on a PC or use internal storage.
No games found. Copy .iso (PS2) or .VCD/.cue (PS1) files to the folder and tap ⚙ › Refresh.
